content:
elaine: FYI customer PicnicHealth is seeing large p95/p99 tail timeouts and intermittent 5xx from the hosted API hitting /v1/generate on model redwood-7b-v2. They started at ~09:12 UTC and are still seeing failures. Logs point to request-queue saturation and continuous-batching backlog. Escalating to incidents.
pj: ack. can you paste the customer request id + sample curl and any request headers? also tenant id if available.
elaine: tenant=tenant-picnic-964, sample curl from customer (redacted token):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-v2","input":"Summarize...","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
```
Response observed: 504 Gateway Timeout or 503 Service Unavailable after 30s. They report p95 latency > 12s and bursts of 5xx during a tenant spike.
Attached customer log snippet: `req=abc123 status=504 q_depth=1200 batching_backlog_ms=4500 host=gateway-12`

infra-bot: Alert: queue_depth high on gateway-12 (metric threshold 800) at 2026-02-18T09:13:02Z. Autoscaler action recommended.

sam: I see gateway-12 had a rapid ingress spike from tenant-picnic-964 around 09:11–09:14, continuous batching queues filled, kv-cache misses increased. Likely continuous batching combining long sequences caused backlog and queue depth cap triggered early rejects.
rick: is this strictly tenant-local (one tenant) or cross-tenant pressure? if tenant-local we can throttle them or route to a dedicated pool temporarily.
oncall: I'm taking lead. first step: admit mitigation. pj, can we temporarily bump the request-queue depth cap for hosted tier (gateway-12) from 1024 -> 2048 for 10m to drain? keep an eye on memory.
pj: we can patch config and trigger a soft restart for the gateway process. doing patch now (will annotate change). also toggling continuous batching from "aggressive" to "latency-optimized" for that gateway to reduce batching latency.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: gateway-config-update v2.3.4 -> modifying request_queue.max_depth for gateway-12. ETA ~45s.
maya: Customer is asking for repro steps and whether this is on their side. They only increased traffic for a scheduled onboarding job but within expected qps. They want credits if we caused downtime.

elaine: told customer we are investigating and will update. asked them to provide a short seq that reproduces.

pj: patch applied, continuous-batching mode set to latency-optimized, queue max_depth increased to 2048. Monitoring for memory pressure. Logs show backlog dropping from ~4500ms to ~300ms and q_depth steadying at ~220.
ops-bot: Noted: temporary config change by pj (ticket INC-22345). Reminder: revert after incident unless follow-up says keep.
sam: early metrics: 5xx rate for tenant-picnic-964 down from 8% -> 0.6%, p95 latency dropped from 12s -> 2.8s after change. However overall gateway CPU spiked +15%.
rick: we should also add a short-term routing rule: route tenant-picnic-964 to a smaller model (redwood-3b-qlora) for non-critical requests and to the larger model only if token budget allows. do we have a policy for per-tenant fallbacks?
oncall: yes, we can add a per-tenant policy via routing table. doing that now for picnic-964; route non-streaming generate calls to redwood-3b-qlora as fallback for 30m.
elaine: sent customer: "We've applied temporary mitigations (queue cap bump + batching mode change + routing fallback). Please verify. We're offering 25% billing credit for affected window while we finish postmortem." customer replied :thumbsup: and said success signal is fewer 504s.

elaine: repro steps we used internally (for records):
1) run a local load generator simulating 600 concurrent small requests + 40 long-run requests to redwood-7b-v2 streaming off.
2) inject entropy to cause KV cache misses (new prompts).
3) observe gateway queue depth and continuous-batching backlog.

Logs captured: 
```
[09:12:22] gateway-12 INFO req=abc123 tenant=picnic-964 q_depth=1204 batching_backlog_ms=4523 action=enqueue
[09:12:55] gateway-12 WARN reject=true req=def456 tenant=picnic-964 reason=queue_overflow
[09:13:07] model-host-7b INFO kv_cache.miss=1 latency=520ms token=345
```

pj: action items:
- A1: Add an automated short-circuit: if tenant queue_depth > 1000 and batching_backlog_ms > 2000, prefer latency-optimized batching mode and trigger per-tenant fallback routing (owner: pj, ETA 48h).
- A2: add a dashboard alert to distinguish tenant-local saturation vs cross-tenant (owner: sam, ETA 24h).
- A3: review default queue max_depth and memory guardrails (owner: infra team, ETA 72h).
- A4: billing: confirm credit to PicnicHealth for 09:10–09:25 UTC (owner: maya, ETA 2h).

maya: billing credit issued note: credit 25% on hosted compute for the window. informing customer now.

oncall: closing mitigation. Please file a short postmortem in /incidents/postmortems and link this thread. Include reproducible runner and config snippet.

pj: config snippet we used to patch gateway: 
```
{"gateway_id":"gateway-12","request_queue":{"max_depth":2048,"reject_threshold":0.95},"batching":{"mode":"latency-optimized","max_batch_tokens":4096}}
```

elaine: thanks everyone. keeping thread open for postmortem items. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-platform for follow-up. :pray:

-- end of thread --
